messages:
Mariam: Quick note from onboarding: the README quickstart has a couple of stale snippets causing friction. New hires keep copy/pasting and then filing auth tickets.
Thom: which snippets are stale?
Mariam: two main issues: 1) env var name mismatch (README and sample-app Dockerfile use different names), 2) SDK constructor examples are old style. In Go example we still show NewClient("TOKEN") but current Go SDK prefers client,err := redwood.FromEnv().
Priya: saw the same in the JS quickstart. It shows `new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })` instead of `Redwood.fromEnv()` and the env var it references is `REDWOOD_KEY`. Our standard is `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
Jules: also, the retry snippet in the doc suggests `retries: 5` generically. That was true pre-v2 semantics. Now retries are idempotent-only unless you opt in with an explicit flag. People assume POST will auto-retry and end up with duplicates.
Mariam: repro steps I recorded: clone quickstart, build container (Dockerfile sets ENV REDWOOD_KEY=...), start, curl POST /chat -> 401. Replace ENV var name or use FromEnv in code and it works.
Thom: is this covered by docs CI? I thought we had a smoke run for copy/paste snippets.
Priya: docs CI only runs markdown lint and link checks. We don't execute snippets. We should add a tiny snippet smoke harness that runs the Node and Go examples with a dummy token and verifies client init path and resulting error codes (401 expected). That would detect env var mismatches and wrong constructor calls.
Jules: good idea. Also, let's add explicit version notes where behavior diverged: Node SDK change v2.1.0 (retry default), Go SDK change v0.9.0 (from constructor to factory). Put a short parenthetical in the quickstart lines.
Mariam: proposed README copy: "Use Redwood.fromEnv()/FromEnv() helpers and set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment. If running in Docker, update the example Dockerfile to expose the same var. Note: SDK retry defaults are idempotent-only starting in Node >= v2.1.0 and Go >= v0.9.0; for non-idempotent ops add an idempotency key or opt-in retry with caution."
Thom: can we show a tiny example for idempotency header? e.g.:```js
// Node
const client = Redwood.fromEnv();
await client.chat.create({ messages }, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': uuidv4() } });
``` and for Go:```go
// Go
client, _ := redwood.FromEnv()
ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), "headers", map[string]string{"Idempotency-Key": uuid.New().String()})
client.Chat.Create(ctx, payload)
```
Priya: let's keep the Go example idiomatic (use context.WithValue is meh) but it communicates the idea. I'll tidy in the PR.
Mariam: I'll open a small docs PR to: update env var in README and sample-app Dockerfile, replace deprecated constructors with FromEnv factories, add idempotency snippet and a short note about retry default with versions, and add a lightweight smoke test in devex/test-snippets that runs examples and asserts they fail fast with 401 when token is wrong.
DocsBot: PR 1987 created by @mariam — includes README updates and test harness. CI queued. :github: 
Thom: ping me when CI is green; I'll do a quick review of the retry wording to avoid promising behavior across minor versions.
Priya: will follow up with a backport to the quickstart branch used by onboarding docs. New hires were blocked for ~20 minutes total across last week by this.
Mariam: thanks all. If we add the smoke test to CI please make sure it runs only in docs CI (use small ephemeral run, no network calls besides hitting local sample-app).
Jules: ack. Also adding a note in the onboarding checklist so TSEs know to check env var if someone reports 401.
Mariam: perfect — will update PR description with checklist items. :white_check_mark:
